# Power BI Build Pack — Customer Churn Analysis

A complete, portable build pack so you can assemble the exact same Power BI report
without proprietary binaries, ODBC drivers, or the pipeline runtime. Everything is
**CSV + markdown + M code**, generated by:

```bash
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset telco --stage powerbi   # data pack CSVs (data/telco/)
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset telco --stage preview    # HTML preview (dashboard_preview_telco.html)
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset bank --stage powerbi     # bank pack (data/bank/)
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset bank --stage preview     # bank preview (dashboard_preview_bank.html)
```

## What's in this folder

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `data/<dataset>/` | **10 CSV files** — the data pack for one dataset (see list below) |
| `01_power_query.m` | Copy-paste M code blocks (one per table) for Power Query |
| `02_data_model.md` | Star-schema diagram, relationships, grain, column dictionary |
| `03_dax_measures.md` | 18 ready-to-paste DAX measures with formatting notes |
| `04_report_layout.md` | 5-page spec with visual types, fields, slicers, theme |
| `connection.txt` | Exact import steps for CSV vs Excel |
| `dashboard_preview_<dataset>.html` | Self-contained browser preview (base64 PNGs) |

## Data pack — 10 CSV files (per dataset)

The 10 files below are produced for **either** `telco` or `bank` and land
under `powerbi/data/<dataset>/`.

| File | Rows | Grain | Key columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dim_customer.csv` | 7,043 (telco) / 10,000 (bank) | 1 row / customer | `customerID` (telco) or `CustomerId` (bank), `tenure`, `Contract`/`Geography`, `MonthlyCharges`, `churn_risk_score`, `surv_prob_at_horizon`, `churn`, `Churn` |
| `dim_tenure.csv` | 73 (telco) / 11 (bank) | 1 row / tenure unit | `tenure_month`, `tenure_band`, `customers`, `churners`, `churn_rate_pct`, `survival_prob` |
| `kpi_churn_by_segment.csv` | 20 (telco) / 9 (bank) | segment × category | `segment`, `group`, `churn_rate`, `count`, `churners` |
| `kpi_tenure_bands.csv` | 7 (telco) / 11 (bank) | tenure band | `tenure_band`, `customers`, `churners`, `churn_rate_pct`, `survival_prob` |
| `kpi_model_comparison.csv` | 2 | model | `model`, `roc_auc`, `pr_auc`, `recall_1`, `precision_1`, `f1_1`, `support_1`, `tn`, `fp`, `fn`, `tp`, `feature_importance` |
| `kpi_survival_summary.csv` | 4 | segment | `group`, `median_survival_time`, `survival_at_12`, `survival_at_24`, `survival_at_36`, `survival_at_48`, `survival_at_60`, `survival_at_72` |
| `kpi_cox_hazards.csv` | 17 (telco) / 10 (bank) | covariate | `covariate`, `hazard_ratio`, `hr_lower_95`, `hr_upper_95`, `p_value`, `concordance`, `coef` |
| `kpi_business_impact.csv` | 1 | KPI | `cap`, `customers_at_risk`, `revenue_at_risk`, `estimated_monthly_profit_lost`, `avg_risk_of_top_cap` |
| `kpi_targeting_lift.csv` | 6 | list size | `list_size`, `churners`, `customers`, `churn_rate_pct`, `avg_risk`, `lift_vs_all_pp` |

> **Telco vs Bank:** re-run the stage with `--dataset bank` to get the bank
> pack. Tables are identical except `dim_customer` has `Geography` instead of
> `Contract`/`PaymentMethod`, and there is no `MonthlyCharges`/`TotalCharges`.

## Quick start (2 minutes)

### Option A — CSV import (recommended, zero dependencies)

1. **Get Data → Text/CSV** → pick the 10 files from `powerbi/data/<dataset>/`
2. In **Power Query Editor**, paste the relevant block from `01_power_query.m`
   into each query's Advanced Editor (or just let PBI auto-detect types and
   manually promote headers).
3. **Manage Relationships** → create **one** relationship:
   `dim_customer[tenure]` (Many) → `dim_tenure[tenure_month]` (One), Single
4. **Modeling → New measure** → paste the 18 measures from `03_dax_measures.md`
5. Build the 5 pages following `04_report_layout.md`

### Option B — Excel workbook (single file, same sheets)

```bash
# The pipeline also writes an Excel with the same tables:
# reports/Churn_Analysis.xlsx (8 sheets, including survival_summary, surv_cox)
```

1. **Get Data → Excel** → `reports/Churn_Analysis.xlsx`
2. Pick the 8 sheets (no `connection.txt`, no `kpi_targeting_lift`)
3. Same relationship + measures + layout

> **Why CSV?** Portable, diff-able in Git, no driver issues, works in
> Power BI Service scheduled refresh (OneDrive / SharePoint) out of the box.

## HTML Preview (no Power BI needed)

Open `dashboard_preview_<dataset>.html` in any browser — it contains:

- All 6 pipeline figures embedded as base64 PNGs (works offline)
- KPI cards with the exact numbers from the pipeline
- Every table rendered with sorting/hover
- Same colour theme and layout as the .pbix spec

This is the **review artifact** for stakeholders who don't have Power BI Desktop.

## Reproducibility

The numbers in this pack come from a **deterministic pipeline**:

```bash
# Full analysis (figures + Excel + model + survival)
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset telco

# Data pack only
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset telco --stage powerbi

# Preview HTML only
python -m src.run_churn_analysis --dataset telco --stage preview
```

Random seed = `42` everywhere (split, gradient boosting). Re-run = identical
CSVs. The pack is a **build artifact**, not a snapshot — regenerate it whenever
the pipeline changes.

## Methodology in one paragraph

The dataset is the IBM Telco Customer Churn (7,043 customers, 26.5% churn).
Tenure in months is the time axis; `churn = 1` means the customer left at that
tenure, `churn = 0` means right-censored (still active). The survival analysis
uses **Kaplan-Meier** curves (non-parametric, no assumptions) and a **Cox
proportional hazards** model (one-hot encoded categoricals, 0.844 concordance).
The classification models (Logistic + Gradient Boosting) ignore censoring and
are biased for time-to-event — they are included for business familiarity and
comparison. Targeting uses the logistic probability score; lift at K = 500 is
≈ 2.02× base rate (telco) / 2.19× (bank), measured on the hold-out test set.
Revenue at risk uses `MonthlyCharges` × churners in top-K.
